cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.title: Weather Watchers Circle
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.objective: Observe outdoors/window weather and record it on the class chart.
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.description: Children look outside, describe sky/air, and place a weather symbol on today’s chart square.
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.materials:
Weather chart
Symbol cards (printable)
Window/door access
Printable (draft): Weather Symbol Cards
Printable (draft): Weekly Weather Observation Chart
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.preparation:
Post chart at child height
Prep today’s blank square
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.steps:
1. Look outside together
2. Share what you notice (sky, wet, wind)
3. Choose a weather symbol
4. Mark warm/cool with a simple choice
5. Predict tomorrow in one word
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.teacherLanguage: What do you observe about today’s weather?
cur-act-2709c6a020ae29a4.observationOpportunities: Describes weather; places symbol; uses weather words.
teacherTips: Do this daily — repetition builds the science habit.

substitutions.use: classroom blocks, paper, or dramatic-play stand-ins

cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.title: Sunshine Movement Game
cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.objective: Move like sunshine with big stretches and shadow play when possible.
cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.description: Children stretch like sun rays, move fast/slow, and notice shadows if sunny.
cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.preparation:
Clear space
If sunny, note shadow wall/floor
cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.steps:
1. Stretch arms like sun rays
2. Move slowly then quickly
3. Make shadows if sunny
4. Drink water after moving
5. Rest in shade pretend spot
cur-act-75e14c8e79726b23.teacherLanguage: Can your arms shine like warm sun rays?
teacherTips: On cloudy days, use flashlight shadow play indoors.

cur-act-5612d85bc9f65bfc.description: Children use cotton, chalk, paint, or torn paper on blue/gray paper however they choose — no sample cloud to copy.

Cotton/fiber fill
Chalk

Smocks

4. Describe your weather art

cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.title: Rain Drop Sensory Investigate
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.objective: Investigate water ‘rain’ with tools and describe how it moves.
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.description: Children drip, pour, and splash in a shallow rain bin using cups, eyedroppers, and waterproof figures.
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.materials:
Shallow water bin
Cups
Eyedroppers/basters
Towels
Smocks
Optional rain stick
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.preparation:
Fill shallow water
Towel floor
Limit participants
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.steps:
1. Listen to rain stick or rain sounds talk
2. Drip water like rain
3. Pour from high/low — what changes?
4. Use words wet/splash/drip
5. Dry hands and reset tools
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.teacherLanguage: What do you notice when the rain falls from higher up?
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.observationOpportunities: Pours with control; uses descriptive words; collaborates.
cur-act-195f18300ada3c7f.safetyNotes: Shallow water only; mop spills; no drinking bin water.
teacherTips: Add ice on hot days for temperature talk.

Scarves
Paper
Feathers (large)

week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers become weather watchers who observe, record, and investigate sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, and stormy weather. Clothing choices, safety, and process art support real outdoor noticing — not elementary meteorology worksheets.
week.objectives:
Observe and describe daily weather using child-friendly vocabulary
Record weather on a simple class chart
Investigate wind, water, and sound through play experiments
Connect weather to clothing and safety choices
Express weather ideas through process art and movement
week.weeklyMaterials:
Weather chart + symbol cards (printable draft)
Clipboards
Pinwheels / scarves / small fan (teacher-controlled)
Water/rain sensory bin tools
Dress-up weather gear
Paint, paper, cotton/cloud materials for process art
Drums/metal pans for thunder sound play
Season/clothing cards (printable draft)
Books about weather
week.familyConnection: Families can share one weather observation at drop-off for the class chart (photo optional).
week.adaptations: Use real photos for support. Indoor alternatives for extreme weather. Accept one-word weather descriptions. Offer hand-over-hand for chart marking.
